\chapter{The People Around You}
\label{ch:te-people}
\hlchaptermodality{88}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can talk about children, a boy or a girl, a person, and a relative when people introduce themselves.}

Complete TE-C88-relative: introduce the people around you.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[pillalu]{\te{పిల్లలు} (pillalu) — children}

\label{lesson:TE-C88-children}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for I see, then the Telugu for really.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{పిల్లలు}}
\textbf{\te{పిల్లలు}} (\emph{pillalu}) — \textquotedblleft{}children\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{పిల్లలు} \te{ఉన్నారా}?} — \textquotedblleft{}do you have children?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}to you, are there children?\textquotedblright{}. The \textbf{-\te{లు}} at the end is the plural you met in your very first lesson.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The question that follows a name in almost every first conversation.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pillalu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pillalu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{mīku pillalu unnārā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for I see, then the Telugu for really, then say \emph{pillalu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{పిల్లలు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Children\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[abbāyi]{\te{అబ్బాయి} (abbāyi) — a boy; a son}

\label{lesson:TE-C88-boy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for really, then the Telugu for children.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అబ్బాయి}}
\textbf{\te{అబ్బాయి}} (\emph{abbāyi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a boy\textquotedblright{}, and in a family, \textquotedblleft{}a son\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మా} \te{అబ్బాయి}} — \textquotedblleft{}our boy\textquotedblright{}, which is how a parent says \textquotedblleft{}my son\textquotedblright{} out loud.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for a boy that doubles as the everyday word for a son.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abbāyi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abbāyi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mā abbāyi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for really, then the Telugu for children, then say \emph{abbāyi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అబ్బాయి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A boy; a son\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ammāyi]{\te{అమ్మాయి} (ammāyi) — a girl; a daughter}

\label{lesson:TE-C88-girl}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for children, then the Telugu for a boy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అమ్మాయి}}
\textbf{\te{అమ్మాయి}} (\emph{ammāyi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a girl\textquotedblright{}, and in a family, \textquotedblleft{}a daughter\textquotedblright{}.

It is built like \textbf{\te{అబ్బాయి}}, and it opens on the same sound as \textbf{\te{అమ్మ}}, \textquotedblleft{}mother\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\te{మా} \te{అమ్మాయి}} — \textquotedblleft{}our girl\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}my daughter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Boy and girl as a pair, each also a word for a child of the family.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ammāyi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ammāyi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mā abbāyi}, then \emph{mā ammāyi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for children, then the Telugu for a boy, then say \emph{ammāyi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అమ్మాయి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A girl; a daughter\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[maniṣi]{\te{మనిషి} (maniṣi) — a person}

\label{lesson:TE-C88-person}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a boy, then the Telugu for a girl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{మనిషి}}
\textbf{\te{మనిషి}} (\emph{maniṣi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a person, a human being\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మంచి} \te{మనిషి}} — \textquotedblleft{}a good person\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\te{మంచి}} you already have. The plural changes shape: \textbf{\te{మనుషులు}} (\emph{manuṣulu}), \textquotedblleft{}people\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for anyone at all, and your first plural that changes its stem.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maniṣi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maniṣi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{manci maniṣi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a boy, then the Telugu for a girl, then say \emph{maniṣi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{మనిషి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A person, a human being\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bandhuvu]{\te{బంధువు} (bandhuvu) — a relative}

\label{lesson:TE-C88-relative}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a girl, then the Telugu for a person.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{బంధువు}}
\textbf{\te{బంధువు}} (\emph{bandhuvu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a relative\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{అతను} \te{మా} \te{బంధువు}} — \textquotedblleft{}he is our relative\textquotedblright{}, with no word for \emph{is}, the same way \textbf{\te{నా} \te{పేరు} ...} needs none.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Children, a boy, a girl, a person, a relative: the people an introduction reaches for.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bandhuvu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bandhuvu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{atanu mā bandhuvu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a girl, then the Telugu for a person, then say \emph{bandhuvu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{బంధువు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A relative\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
